libcontainer: Separate cgroup configuration from creation This adds the ability to set the owner of the parent cgroups, this is needed when entering a cgroup namespace as the subdirectories and their files must be owned by the user that root maps to outside the container. Move cgroup creation from where the config is created until later. This information isn't known by login manager when creating the container. Moving it later allows it to be configured like other config options. BUG=none TEST=run with dependent changes and see that the cgroup is created with the correct owner and at the correct place in the cgroup hierarchy. Change-Id: Ia31fb7eebe562b36216ce547c9889bcffba7f257 Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362097 Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

login: Set cgroup parent directory for android containers Android will now run in a new cgroup namespace. This will allow it to modify its own cgroups while not knowing that it is part of a larger cgroup hierarchy. Configure the external cgroup "session_manager_containers" that will be the root of Android's cgroup namespace. BUG=b/29259708 TEST=Start android and check that it is in a new cgroup namespace rooted at session_manager_containers. libcontainer: Run containers in a cgroup namespace Now that all of our supported kernels support cgroup namespaces, enable them when running a container. This will allow the container to modify cgroup parameters for sub groups but still allows the system to control overall limits. The contained processes will not know that it is in a cgroup namespace, it appears as the root inside the namespace. reef: Enable PMIC after 3.3V This changes the ordering of rail/PMIC init slightly so that the 3.3V rail comes up before the PMIC, which follows the ordering in the PMIC datasheet for cold booting. The way we did it earlier was to avoid interrupt storms caused by powering the SoC's GPIO block with SLP signals before powering the PMIC. However the PMIC ignores the SLP signals when it's first enabled, so while the suprious interrupts were visible on the scope it's unlikely that the software was affected. OTOH, as Kevin pointed out in CL:358913 enabling the PMIC before the 3.3V causes a race condition whereby the PMIC may fault. BUG=chrome-os-partner:51323 BRANCH=none TEST=built and booted on EVT Signed-off-by: Rachel Nancollas <rachelsn@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Change-Id: I6eb734f0600daa5de0d970ce228cf3e7ec97d01d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/372344 Commit-Ready: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Tested-by: David Hendricks <dhendrix@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kevin K Wong <kevin.k.wong@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Shawn N <shawnn@chromium.org>

Update Brltty to version 5.4. The upstream Gentoo package is currently on Brltty-5.2, but we require Brltty-5.4 to pick up support for a few new braille displays. This upgrades us from 4.5. This cl makes the necessary changes to metadata.xml/manifest and adds a new ebuild for 5.4. Summary of changes to patches against 5.4: - the following patches were rebased from brltty-4.5-*.patch brltty-5.4-tty0-openflags.patch brltty-5.4-supress-messages.patch brltty-5.4-udev-run-script.patch - Already committed upstream in brltty-5.4: brltty-4.5-remove-umask.patch brltty-4.5--updusbdevs.patch brltty-4.5-socket-path.patch brltty-4.5-fix-mk4build.patch (upstream is slightly different regex, but achieves the same case insensitive match). These two patches are upstream support for specific displays; they do not apply cleanly on brltty-5.4, so there were likely changes to these displays since the cherrypicks. We should test these displays specifically: brltty-4.5-handytech.patch The following patch appears to work around an issue with Seka displays; try not applying this patch to re-enable support brltty-4.5-udev.patch BUG=chromium:637952 TEST=A basic test (output/input, hardware keys) was done for: - Freedom Scientific Focus Blue 40 (first gen) - Papenmeier EL80c - VarioUltra 20 Change-Id: I983a0b04bd06e00d0c66f48d37875cb8d1d7b8d8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/372318 Commit-Ready: David Tseng <dtseng@chromium.org> Tested-by: David Tseng <dtseng@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Cr50: Use parse_bool() for boolean args The parse_bool() function exists so we don't have to litter our console commands with stuff like this: if (!strncasecmp(argv[1], "on") || !strncasecmp(argv[1], "enable" || !strncasecmp(argv[1], "true" || [...] This CL uses parse_bool instead of that kind of thing so I don't have to remember which commands use "enable" and which use "on" and so forth. cr50: remove internal pull up on DIOM0 There is leakage on SYS_RST_ODL from the internal pullup cr50 has on DIOM0. This change removes the internal pullup. Without the internal pull up SYS_RST_ODL is not pulled up whenever the EC is off. I changed how sys_rst_asserted is handled so it will ignore the sys_rst interrupt whenever rbox asserts EC_RST to make sure cr50 doesn't reset itself every time it resets the EC. If the EC resets itself and sys_rst_l is no longer pulled up, it is fine if cr50 resets.
